AI-Generated Summary
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open, customizable multimodal model with a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture that activates 12B parameters per token for agentic workflows.
The model combines reasoning, instruction following, tool use, and text, image, document, and video understanding in a single model, eliminating the need for separate vision-language models.
On a single GPU, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL delivers up to 5x higher throughput for agentic tasks compared to other open models in its size category.
Organizations including Scale AI, Ramp, and AI21 have post-trained the model for specialized workflows, achieving improvements such as 40x lower inference cost, 10x lower latency, and 40% higher accuracy.
Developers can customize the model using NVIDIA NeMo with supervised fine-tuning, low-rank adaptation, and reinforcement learning on open datasets released on Hugging Face.
The model uses LiLiCorr speculative decoding, NVFP4 quantization with quantization-aware distillation, multi-token prediction, and context reuse to optimize inference efficiency on platforms including NVIDIA DGX Spark.
Next Steps
Read the Nemotron 3.5 technical report for model details.
Explore the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL usage cookbook on GitHub for customization resources.
Get started with NVIDIA NIM for optimized deployment.
Powered by NVIDIA Nemotron. AI-generated content may summarize information incompletely. Verify important information. Learn more
Always-on agents are taking on longer, more complex enterprise workflows. A single request can involve reading a document, checking information across sources, following company policy, and calling several tools.
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open, customizable multimodal model for these specialized workflows. Its 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture activates 12B parameters per token, balancing model capacity with inference efficiency.
On a single GPU, this model delivers up to 5x higher throughput for agentic tasks compared to other open models in its size category.
Figure 1. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL delivers over 600 TPS on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index agentic tasks on the Baseten endpoint
The model combines reasoning, instruction following, and tool use with text, image, document, and video understanding. By combining these capabilities into one model, teams can handle text and visual tasks without deploying separate text and vision-language models or passing task context between them.
Developers can post-train Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with NVIDIA NeMo using their own data, tools, policies, and workflows. This post explains how to use that foundation to build specialized enterprise agents and describes the training and inference techniques that power it.
Why Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for specialized agents?
Agents need to understand both their tasks and operating environments. A customer-service agent must follow company return policies. Research agents connect evidence across sources, while document agents interpret tables, charts, and page layouts.
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL combines reasoning and visual understanding across a range of agent workflows, including:
Coding: Test and validate code, analyze errors, and recommend fixes.
Web research: Search across websites, connect information, and verify answers.
Document intelligence: Extract information from tables, charts, and page layouts to produce summaries and reports.
Cybersecurity: Identify security vulnerabilities and triage threats to prioritize remediation.
Video understanding: Extract information for search, content review, and incident analysis.
Within a system of models, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL handles specialized, multistep work that needs reasoning, tool use, and text and visual understanding together. Smaller models, such as NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, handle high-volume text tasks, while frontier models such as NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra tackle complex planning and orchestration.
Customize Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for domain data, tools, and policies
Specialized agents must learn how an organization works. Domain terminology, tool interfaces, operating procedures, and policy requirements shape how agents complete tasks successfully.
Organizations in industries ranging from cybersecurity and finance to healthcare are post-training Nemotron 3.5 Super VL to outperform frontier models in accuracy and efficiency across their production workflows. For example:
Scale AI, an AI data and technology provider, post-trained Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for automated vendor credit processing at Skydance Corporation, a media and entertainment company. Inference cost for this workload will decrease by 40x and latency by 5x.
Ramp, a financial operations platform provider, is converting receipt images into structured JSON containing merchant information, dates, and payment data. Ramp expects up to 50% higher throughput and 10x lower latency.
AI21 and Alice post-trained Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for threat intelligence and vulnerability analysis, improving accuracy by 41%.
Figure 2. Post-trained Nemotron 3.5 Super VL achieves leading performance for specialized tasks across industries
Teams can use NVIDIA NeMo open libraries to post-train models to meet these requirements. Developers can use NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to teach domain-specific behavior. Reinforcement learning (RL) improves performance in agentic environments that reflect organizational workflows.
Alongside Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, NVIDIA is releasing open datasets on Hugging Face. These include agentic tool-use and conversational data, finance reasoning and tool-calling datasets, instruction-following and chat data, long-context transduction and translation data, fairness data, and 40 vision-language datasets. These datasets can supplement proprietary data for SFT and RL.
For multimodal data, start with NeMo Data Designer resources for chart question answering and long-document understanding. Explore NVIDIA NeMo RL and NVIDIA NeMo Gym for RL and environment-based evaluation.
Organizations can adapt and deploy the model’s open weights in supported local, data center, or cloud environments to meet their infrastructure and data requirements. For customization resources, see the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL usage cookbook on GitHub.
Combine text and visual understanding in one workflow
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL combines text, image, document, and video understanding with reasoning and instruction following to answer questions across these inputs.
Its visual training covers charts, tables, optical character recognition (OCR), multipage documents, and video understanding. A two-stage SFT pipeline trains the language and vision components, combining visual evidence with reasoning, chat, safety, long-context data, and agent trajectories.
For document intelligence, the same model can interpret a chart, connect it with a table elsewhere in a document, and summarize both. Developers can tailor the workflow to their own documents and evaluation criteria.
Diverse training data generated with NeMo Data Designer helped the model better understand complex charts. On CharXiv, a chart-reasoning benchmark, the model scored 80.8%, compared with 63% for Nemotron 3 Nano Omni. With Python code interpretation, it reached 84%. For the approach and lessons learned, read the chart-understanding deep dive and the open-source chart question-answering pipeline.
This model was built with support and expertise from Nemotron Coalition organizations. For instance, high-quality datasets from Perplexity helped improve and streamline the model’s mid-training. Environments from Prime Intellect enabled building better teacher models.
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is also one of the top open models on the OCRBench v2 leaderboard.
Accuracy and efficiency across agent tasks
Evaluations of Nemotron 3.5 Super VL span Hermes, LangChain, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Pi, Codex, and Claude. In addition to coding tasks, agent harness providers use their own evaluations to test a wide range of agent tasks. On Hermes Bench and LangChain behavioral evaluations, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL scores higher than Nemotron 3 Ultra.
ModelHermes BenchLangChain EvalsNemotron 3 Ultra56.33%84.3%Nemotron 3.5 Super VL63.44%87.05%Table 1. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL scores higher than Nemotron 3 Ultra on Hermes Bench and LangChain evaluations
For always-on agents, efficiency determines how much work a deployment can complete. Throughput, token usage, tool calls, and the steps needed to reach a correct result all affect task completion time.
Figure 3. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL uses higher throughput and token efficiency to deliver 4x faster task completion
This model was also optimized to run locally on NVIDIA DGX Spark. An independent evaluation by EXO Labs placed Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on the Pareto frontier for accuracy and task completion time.
Figure 4. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL balances accuracy and speed for agent tasks on DGX Spark
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL under the hood
The model builds on a strong foundation and uses a hybrid architecture, speculative decoding, context reuse, and mixed precision to reduce inference work across repeated agent calls.
Building a strong base model
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra. Ultra’s coding capabilities, combined with the SkewReverse loss used during distillation, helped improve coding accuracy.
During post-training, multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) combines guidance from specialized teachers across text and vision. The model generates responses, and the teachers score them for video reasoning and tracking, vision tool use, and alignment.
Additional training on examples of agent actions, code repositories, and software engineering tasks improved the model’s performance on agent tasks. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL outperforms Nemotron 3 Super on SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench across multiple evaluation setups.
Continued pretraining with high-quality natural and synthetic data improved Indic-language capabilities and contributed to higher overall scores after post-training. This stage added 10B Indic tokens, drawn from a 12-language subset of Nemotron-pretraining-Indic-v1 and natural Indic text.
NVIDIA is releasing the full dataset, which contains about 2.8T tokens across 22 Indian languages and was developed with IIT Madras and its AI4Bharat lab. The following results are based on the post-trained Nemotron 3.5 Super VL.
Figure 5. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL delivers leading accuracy on Indic benchmarks, thanks to specialized Indic data
Developers can use NeMo to build on this foundation and customize Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for their applications, adapting its reasoning and agentic capabilities to their data, tools, and workflows.
LiLiCorr: An open speculative decoding technique
LiLiCorr improves parallel speculative decoding by jointly evaluating token candidates across an entire draft, capturing dependencies that independent token predictions miss. A lightweight network computes compatibility scores in a single pass to produce more coherent drafts, leaving only a low-cost, sequential final selection step.
On DGX Spark, LiLiCorr is the recommended drafter for low-latency inference with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL. It delivers up to 2.3x faster token generation than decoding without speculation.
NVFP4 and mixed precision
The model uses NVIDIA Model Optimizer for post-training quantization and quantization-aware distillation (QAD). The NVFP4 recipe uses 4-bit weights and activations on the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture. The same checkpoint runs on non-Blackwell platforms with 4-bit weights and 16-bit activations. Precision is selected separately for sensitive components.
NVFP4 makes the model smaller, and QAD helps it retain its accuracy at lower precision. During QAD, the quantized model learns to match the outputs of the original BF16 model, which closes the accuracy gap that quantization introduces. QAD also supports storing the key-value (KV) cache in NVFP4 instead of FP8 while still meeting accuracy targets. Because QAD happens during training, it adds no inference overhead.
Multi-token prediction
Multi-token prediction (MTP) gives Nemotron 3.5 Super VL an internal drafter that proposes several tokens for the main model to verify in one forward pass. Accepting multiple tokens at once reduces the number of compute-intensive verification steps needed to generate a response.
A dedicated MTP-boosting training phase further aligned the drafter with the final model.
Context reuse across agent turns
Agents repeatedly pass system instructions, tool definitions, and conversation history back to the model. Prefix caching reuses computation from those shared inputs.
The model’s serving optimizations preserve both attention caches and Mamba recurrent states. Additional Mamba checkpoints reduce the replay needed to recover inputs for speculative decoding, while internal checkpointing avoids extra model passes during prompt processing.
Simplify production deployment with NVIDIA NIM and NVIDIA Dynamo
NVIDIA NIM packages models with optimized inference engines, validated configurations, and standard APIs for cloud and data center deployment. NIM receives ongoing security, feature, and performance updates. Enterprise support is available through NVIDIA AI Enterprise. Get started with NIM.
NVIDIA Dynamo supports distributed inference optimizations to increase throughput and reduce latency, including KV-cache-aware routing, KV cache management, and disaggregated serving.
On 16 NVIDIA B200 GPUs at 50 tokens per second per user, KV-aware routing with session affinity and KV cache offload serves up to 8x as many users while reducing first-token latency by 85%. Get started with the Dynamo deployment recipes.
Figure 6. NVIDIA Dynamo serves 8x as many users and reduces first-token latency by 85% at the same per-user token rate
Get started with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
Build specialized agents with multimodal reasoning and tool use. Customize the model for specialized workflows, then deploy it in a supported environment.
The release includes base, post-trained, and NVFP4-quantized checkpoints with training recipes, data, and reinforcement-learning environments.
See the Nemotron 3.5 technical report for model details and Hugging Face or ModelScope for deployment instructions. For hosted model access, see OpenRouter.

articles.title: 英伟达黄仁勋称 AI 芯片需求持续超过供应能力：几乎每天都有新订单涌入
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋表示，客户对人工智能芯片的订购量持续超过公司的供货能力；即便当前科技股遭遇大幅抛售，引发了市场对采购方如何为该行业巨额扩张筹措资金的质疑，强劲的需求势头依然未减。
在周四播出的 BG2 播客专访中，黄仁勋透露，新订单“几乎每周、每天都在持续涌入”。
我们一直在不断提升供给，但未交付的订单量仍在持续走高。
头部云服务商、新兴 AI 云算力运营商以及硬件设备制造商均已下达了巨额订单。黄仁勋称，客户的需求预测普遍提前至少一年，其中体量最大的客户规划周期甚至排到了两年之后。
然而，英伟达当前分配给这些客户的实际配额，仍远少于其实际需求。黄仁勋指出，电力供应紧张、数据中心尚未完工以及制造元器件短缺，同样是限制公司加速扩充供给的关键瓶颈。
IT之家注意到，针对外界认为 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等公司必须产生足以覆盖数万亿美元 AI 基建投入之巨额收入的担忧，黄仁勋反驳称：“人们对目前的行业现状存在误解。”
据黄仁勋估算，前沿人工智能实验室仅占英伟达整体计算需求的大约 25% 至 30%，其余需求广泛来源于传统计算架构升级、初创团队以及专有商业应用的开发企业。
黄仁勋强调：“他们完全不需要做到上万亿美元的营收规模，就足以证明自身的成功。”

articles.title: Did Anthropic Miss Its Peak IPO Moment?
articles.text:
It’s beginning to look like Anthropic waited too late to go public. Third-quarter revenue numbers disclosed to investors on Wednesday implied that its growth has slowed from the second quarter, which we reported is likely to put a ceiling on its IPO valuation. Anthropic might have been better off going public in June, when its growth was still spectacular. (Of course, a June IPO might have been impractical given that that’s when SpaceX went public.)
As things stand now, Anthropic’s slowing growth may remind investors of a longstanding question surrounding the company: How much of a moat does it really have? Yes, its AI models are as good as they get, but increasingly, businesses don’t need really expensive frontier models. As we wrote earlier this week, developers are increasingly opting for other models that are good enough for most tasks. Anthropic’s aggressive pricing has prompted companies such as Microsoft to cut its spending on the former’s models, we reported 10 days ago. (This trend seems to be spreading).

articles.title: iPhone Duo开启预售：15999元起 首批货源被黄牛炒上天
articles.text:
快科技10月16日消息，苹果首款折叠屏iPhone Duo将在今天晚上8点开启预售。国行起售价为15999元，顶配2TB版本定价26499元，成为苹果史上定价最高的iPhone，并提供星光白色和夜空色两款颜色。
在硬件配置上，iPhone Duo采用书本式折叠方案，属于阔折叠形态。内屏为7.6英寸，并采用屏下摄像头技术；外屏为5.4英寸。
核心搭载台积电2nm工艺的A20 Pro芯片，配备钛合金铰链，整机重量为254克。该机仅支持eSIM，无实体卡槽，也没有长焦镜头和Face ID，解锁方式为侧边指纹识别。
作为苹果首款折叠屏，产能紧张是这款新机面临的最大挑战。产业链人士称，iPhone Duo整机良率目前仅有60%多，量产爬坡缓慢，首发备货量十分有限。目前仅国内单一电商平台预约人数已突破200万，巨大的供需缺口也催生了黄牛市场，首批现货价格被炒上天。
据了解，iPhone Duo的加价方式主要有三种：一是加价幅度在5000元左右，但不能保证到货时间；二是首发当天拿货，加价高达1万元，只为满足首销当天拿到新机的用户。
三是代抢服务，服务费200到1000元不等，且明确“跑单不退”。多位黄牛声称，10月16日的预约位置已满。
种种迹象表明，iPhone Duo将是今年最难抢的苹果手机，也是一款“理财产品”。对于想要第一时间入手的用户来说，除了拼手速，可能还需要做好面对溢价的心理准备。

An update on independent evaluators
Oct 15, 2026
Last month, we committed to stronger independent, third-party assessment of our models and safety practices. We also signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, in which companies pledged to partner with independent external auditors or evaluators. Today, we’re announcing that we’ve started to give employee-like access to a team from METR, a nonprofit that evaluates frontier AI models.
METR will publish the results of its risk assessments. Over the past year, we’ve worked with METR on several reviews of our Risk Reports. We’re also working with SecureBio and Accenture as evaluators, and are in early discussions with several other organizations, including Hugging Face.
Here, we explain our approach to working with evaluators.
Why we work with independent evaluators
As models have become more powerful, they’ve required stronger safeguards and more challenging risk assessments. We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making. But we can’t publicly share all the information relevant to our safety work. Some of it could be useful to malicious actors, or is commercially sensitive, like compute or training information. Instead, we’re giving third-party evaluators deep access to our information, and are having them share evidence and reasoned conclusions about the risks involved in building our models. We aim to close the gap between what evaluators understand about a frontier AI company’s systems and what the company itself understands.
To evaluate frontier models, evaluators need the following:
Expertise in assessing the capabilities of frontier models, including understanding the way evaluations can go wrong, such as alignment faking.
Independence: they shouldn’t hold equity in the company they’re evaluating, or be financially or operationally dependent on it.
Enough access to meaningfully evaluate risks. Beyond access to the latest models, evaluators also need visibility into how those models were trained, into how our safeguards function, and more.
Freedom to publish observations and assessments of a model or a process.
Although the analogy isn’t exact, bank supervision operates on similar logic. Banks know more about their own risk positions than outsiders do, so regulators assign resident examiners to work inside the largest banks. If a bank’s risk-taking could threaten the public, third parties try to see that in advance.
For the AI industry, this is a step toward robust safety oversight. We’re moving quickly with multiple evaluators and learning actively about what kinds of partnership work. We’re committed to sharing updates as we go.
What we mean by “employee-like access”
We’ve onboarded six METR employees with company hardware, office space, and access to internal tools and systems that are roughly on par with what our own risk assessment teams have access to. Outside a small number of clearly defined categories (e.g., data about customers, attorney-client privileged information, or information about our model architectures), Anthropic employees are encouraged to share information with them just as they would with a fellow employee working on alignment risk.1
METR will publish its analysis of our risk levels, incidents, or practices. Anthropic can’t veto publication, but we can require them to redact information if it falls into narrow, predefined categories like the ones above. METR is free to characterize our redactions publicly, and say whether it believes the redactions were justified, as long as it does so without revealing the redacted information.
Our engagement with METR is limited to a small team operating under enforceable agreements. Other METR employees are siloed from that team’s work, including researchers who work with us on other projects. Embedded evaluation gives a few qualified people working under Anthropic’s security standards a close view of how we operate. It’s not a way for other organizations to obtain our information, or that of our customers and partners.
Our other evaluator partnerships
We’re working on several other partnerships. Because these other partnerships are still in early stages, we’re providing these evaluators with more limited information, and they have more limited publication rights. Our goal with these early engagements is to make sure that our partners protect confidential information and have the requisite resources and expertise to evaluate our models. As partnerships progress and we build trust, we hope to fully embed more independent evaluators.
We’re developing three tiers of access for evaluators. Over time, we hope to have several evaluators at the third tier, with each team publishing their own analysis of our risk posture and key decisions.
In the first tier, evaluators conduct narrowly scoped risk investigations. We decide what access to provide a first-tier evaluator, and evaluators can publish their findings with our approval.
In the second tier, evaluators can publish without our approval, and they have access to more information. We can still require removal of specific categories of information, though evaluators can publish their views on whether our redactions were justified.
The third tier is the arrangement we’ve described with METR, with employee-like access and publication rights similar to those of the second tier.
SecureBio is in the process of reviewing the chemical and biological weapons chapter of our August Risk Report, after completing and publishing a pilot review of our previous risk report. After this review is complete, we will consider moving to projects with increased access.2
With Accenture and Faculty, we're working toward an ambitious partnership that includes evaluating and red-teaming models, conducting alignment assessments, testing model safeguards, and building capabilities across our organizations.
We’re embedding evaluators voluntarily, and we believe every frontier AI company should do the same.
Footnotes
Because these evaluators (like bank examiners) may also work with other companies, we exercise caution around the possibility of inadvertent leaks. Information about architectures presents a high risk of inadvertent leaks, and its relevance to risk assessment is typically low. When it is highly relevant, we will generally seek to share it, though this will require explicit internal approvals.

articles.title: The Nordics and NVIDIA Show What’s Possible When a Region Commits to Advanced Computing
articles.text:
The Nordic countries have become the European leader in unicorn startup density, producing the most emerging companies valued at $1 billion or more per capita on the continent.
Now, a new chapter for the region is unfolding as countries race to build one of Europe’s most consequential technology ecosystems.
The many computing advancements already underway in the Nordics, combined with the opportunity that lies ahead, signal a region moving from ambition to application.
NVIDIA’s Investments in the Nordics
Over the past year, NVIDIA has invested in the technology ecosystem in the Nordics, including Sweden’s leading startups Lovable and Legora.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
Lovable, a Stockholm-based startup, provides a software creation platform that enables anyone to build and run software using plain language. In collaboration with NVIDIA, Lovable is optimizing inference for open models and training its models using NVIDIA Dynamo software and Nemotron tools.
Legora provides an agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review and drafting across complex matters.
Nordics Emerge as Infrastructure Hub
The foundation for establishing the Nordics as a technology powerhouse is already being built and the region holds a structural advantage: abundant renewable energy, rigorous data governance and a research tradition that bridges academia and industry.
The Nordics are one of Europe’s fastest growing hubs for infrastructure. AI clouds are expanding with a projected 1 gigawatts of capacity to be deployed across the region by the end of 2027. Among these cloud providers are Bitdeer, CoreWeave, Crusoe, Hyperstack, Nscale, Verda and Volta.
In Sweden, a consortium anchored by Ericsson, AstraZeneca, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments, with SKF as strategic partner, launched Sferical One — a shared supercomputer running on two NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs with 16 racks of NVIDIA DGX GB300 systems and 1,152 GPUs. The consortium will build services using NVIDIA Nemotron open models, which allow researchers to customize and deploy their models in a secure environment.
Nordic-Built Intelligence
Some of the Nordics’ leading technology companies are now building proprietary intelligence on NVIDIA infrastructure.
Spotify, which personalizes music, podcasts and audiobooks for hundreds of millions of listeners, uses NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM inference software to run AI-powered podcast recommendations faster and cheaper at scale. The deployment is a case study in inference efficiency: delivering the same recommendations to a global audience at a lower cost per query.
ABB Robotics developed RobotStudio HyperReality using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bridge the gap between robot simulations and real-world performance. By combining NVIDIA’s advanced simulation capabilities with ABB Robotics’ virtual controller, running the same firmware as its physical robots, the solution enables engineers to train, test and validate robots virtually, while using real-world data to continuously improve the digital model. According to ABB Robotics, the solution delivers up to 99% simulation accuracy and reduces commissioning time by up to 80%.
Finnish telecom company Elisa is launching a beta of Moontalk AIRI, a real-time enterprise agentic assistant that retrieves information, captures insights and documents decisions during meetings and calls. Built on NVIDIA Nemotron open models and distributed infrastructure, it uses company data and low-latency networking to deliver fast, context-aware responses.
Nordic Startups Scaling on NVIDIA
Sweden’s startup ecosystem raised $2.8 billion in the first half of 2026 and is projected to reach $5 billion for the year. This next generation is building fast — and on open models.
Stilta is reinventing how companies protect their inventions with intellectual property. The Stockholm-based startup is post-training NVIDIA Nemotron open models to scale patent analysis from a single patent to entire portfolios — work that was previously out of reach. Nemotron gives Stilta the language model accuracy for continuous portfolio monitoring at scale, across the thousands of patents that large industrial and technology companies hold.
ConfidentialMind’s SampoTron, built on NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Embed, delivers more than 20% improvement in cross-lingual retrieval accuracy across English, Finnish and Swedish.
Agaton, a platform that analyzes customer conversations in real time, is using NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning to speed up Revenue Mining solution on live sales calls. By routing knowledge retrieval to Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, Agaton can cut response latency to deliver fast responses that inform customers’ buying decisions.
Klang, a Swedish speech lab, fine-tuned the NVIDIA Parakeet v3 model to create Pianissimo — a Swedish transcription model that reduces errors by 75% while being 64x faster than the most accurate alternative. Built on over 50,000 hours of Swedish speech using the open source NVIDIA NeMo framework, the model is freely available on Hugging Face.
Embedl, founded in Gothenburg and a member of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups, and Space Cargo Unlimited unveiled an onboard prototype that monitors protein crystallization, flags anomalies and recommends actions on a single NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module, without continuous ground connectivity.
Sweden AI Factory — one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories — announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises across industries, including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming.
Autonomous Machines on Nordic Roads and Factory Floors
In Sweden, advanced computing is also powering vehicles on the road and machines in factories.
Volvo Cars is combining its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with NVIDIA Hyperion, Halos OS and Alpamayo Stack to enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door.
Autonomous freight company Einride is building its next-generation Einride Driver on NVIDIA Hyperion for autonomous freight trucks, using the NVIDIA Halos safety system and NVIDIA Cosmos open world models.
Meanwhile, Toyota Material Handling Europe — the world’s leading forklift manufacturer — is bringing autonomous machines to factory floors. In a collaboration with NVIDIA and SoftServe, Toyota Material Handling Europe is adopting a simulation-first approach to autonomous material handling, cutting autonomous solution deployment time by up to 50% across its global engineering, manufacturing and innovation teams.
Norrsken Foundation and NVIDIA are opening the Stockholm AI Lab, a physical hub for AI-native founders working on global challenges, set to open in 2027.
Quantum Meets Accelerated Computing
Finally, Swedish companies are advancing quantum research using NVIDIA’s quantum computing platform.
Stockholm-based FirstQFM used NVIDIA accelerated computing to train a model that reduces the execution time of quantum processors by 33% without sacrificing performance. Validated on a QuantWare quantum processor unit, this model optimizes how the operations needed by quantum algorithms are turned into detailed hardware instructions, accounting for detailed updates on how the hardware is calibrated.
Tune in to NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin keynote on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 11 a.m. CEST.

articles.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.19247v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs. We actually show that the ability of LLMs to copy in context can be improved through explicit modeling. We propose Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which add a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the conventional language modeling (LM) head. CPLMs improve training efficiency, downstream performance, and offer new operating points in long-context and retrieval setups. We validate our approach by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, showing improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overheads. We explain the success of CPLMs by showing that they partially mitigate the LM head gradient bottleneck through an alternative gradient path.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Multilingual Abstractive Summarization: A Comprehensive Study of English and Bengali
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.19003v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Abstractive summarization remains challenging across languages, where linguistic quality and factual consistency may diverge, particularly in low-resource settings. We present a standardized zero-shot benchmark of eight closed-source and open-weight LLMs on size-matched English and Bengali XL-Sum test sets. Our evaluation combines lexical and semantic metrics with reference-free factuality verification and multidimensional LLM-as-a-Judge assessment, providing a comprehensive analysis of both surface-level quality and factual reliability in multilingual summarization. Results reveal substantial cross-lingual variation: GPT-5.6 Luna leads several English lexical metrics but does not maintain the same advantage in Bengali, where LLaMA 3.3 70B achieves the highest ROUGE and BLEU scores. Gemini 2.5 Flash obtains the highest observed Bengali factuality score. Furthermore, evaluation methods produce different model rankings, highlighting the limitations of relying on a single metric for multilingual summarization assessment. These findings demonstrate that strong English summarization performance does not necessarily transfer to Bengali and emphasize the need for comprehensive evaluation frameworks for low-resource languages.

articles.title: Evaluating Compressed Memory: Dependence, Utility, and Content Benefit
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.19373v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Does a language model answer better because its compressed memory contains useful document information? Replacing memory vectors with zeros can lower a trained model's score without showing that it outperforms a model trained without memory. We combine zeroing with separately trained models that cannot access stored text or receive the same constant input for every document. Across nine systems, some models rely on memory yet perform worse than the trained alternative. For example, in experiments that predict states in generated stories, zeroing memory worsens a model's prediction loss, yet a model trained without memory achieves lower loss than the original model with intact memory. On TriviaQA, giving xRAG memory from another question's passage raises F1, which measures word overlap with accepted answers, from 19.38 without a document to 24.78. Its effect on how often outputs contain an accepted answer is statistically uncertain. The question's retrieved passage scores higher still (29.88 F1). Thus a gain over no document alone does not establish that the gain requires the question's passage. Evaluations must therefore specify the comparison model, absolute performance, and generation and scoring conditions.

articles.title: Bringing ExecuTorch to Arm Cortex-M CPUs
articles.text:
TL;DR
Deploying PyTorch models on microcontrollers has historically required converting to other framework formats, maintaining separate toolchains, and debugging cross-framework numerical mismatches. ExecuTorch eliminates this conversion step entirely.
The Cortex-M backend enables PyTorch models to run directly on Arm Cortex-M CPUs with Arm CMSIS-NN acceleration. It supports all capability tiers (Scalar, DSP, and MVE/Helium) from a single workflow.
We benchmark four of the five models from the MLPerf Tiny suite on the Alif Ensemble E8. Each model runs in 21.5 ms or less and uses under 90 KiB of RAM on a single Cortex-M55 core.
For heterogeneous SoCs, the Cortex-M backend also provides the CPU execution path alongside Ethos-U NPU delegation.
Minimal binary footprint. The ExecuTorch core runtime is under 20 KiB of flash, and operator selective build links only the operators your model needs, so total code size scales with the model rather than the framework.
Background
Microcontrollers power billions of always-on devices: wearables, industrial sensors, voice interfaces, and smart home appliances. These devices operate under extreme constraints: often less than 1 MB of SRAM, single-digit megabytes of flash, and power budgets measured in milliwatts. Despite these limitations, there’s growing demand to run meaningful ML workloads on these platforms and the hardware is evolving to meet it. Modern Cortex-M based microcontroller units (MCUs) now include DSP & vector ISAs, large tightly-coupled memories (TCMs), and power-efficient NPUs such as the Arm Ethos-U NPU that make ML inference more practical in resource constrained devices.
Until now, deploying ML on Cortex-M meant leaving the PyTorch ecosystem. Developers had to convert models to alternative formats, maintain separate toolchains for training and deployment, and debug numerical mismatches introduced during conversion. For teams that train in PyTorch, which accounts for over 90% of the research code published at top ML conferences, this translation step adds friction to every iteration cycle.
ExecuTorch was designed to eliminate this gap. Arm MCU support has been available through the Ethos-U NPU, and the Cortex-M backend extends it to Cortex-M CPUs, so a model can run on parts with or without an accelerator. The trained PyTorch model is exported, quantized and lowered for the device within the same stack that serves models on mobile, desktop and server.
The Cortex-M Backend
The ExecuTorch Cortex-M backend replaces standard PyTorch operators with CMSIS-NN-backed custom operators through ahead-of-time compiler passes. At inference time, these operators call directly into Arm’s CMSIS-NN library, an open source collection of optimized neural network kernels for Cortex-M processors.
Key properties:
CMSIS-NN accelerated. Quantized operations (linear, conv, add, mul, softmax, activations, etc.) are replaced with optimized implementations that call CMSIS-NN functions and additional optimized Cortex-M implementations directly.
Target-aware compilation. The CPU variant (M0 through M85) and ISA tier are specified at compile time, so the correct CMSIS-NN backend is selected, eliminating runtime dispatch overhead.
Purpose-built quantizer. Produces INT8 quantized graphs matching the data layout requirements of CMSIS-NN kernels, using PyTorch’s PT2E quantization framework.
Single compiler toolchain. The Cortex-M lowering path operates directly on the ExecuTorch edge dialect, keeping the compilation pipeline simple and debuggable.
Cortex-M Capability Tiers
The backend targets the full Cortex-M spectrum:
Tier
Cores
Key Feature
Use Case
Scalar
M0, M0+, M3, M23
Standard ARM instructions
Ultra-low-cost, minimal silicon
DSP
M4, M7, M33, M35P
SIMD multiply-accumulate
Mid-range MCUs, signal processing
MVE (aka Helium)
M55, M85
128-bit vector ops, beat-based execution
High-performance MCU ML inference
Arm Helium technology is where the biggest performance gains are. CMSIS-NN leverages Helium’s beat-based execution model to pipeline data movement and compute, providing significant throughput gains for the depthwise and pointwise convolutions common in edge ML architectures. That said, the same workflow targets all variants. The target configuration selects the appropriate backend automatically.
ExecuTorch is Embedded Friendly
Unlike mobile or cloud environments that must accommodate varied hardware at runtime, microcontroller deployments target a fixed hardware profile. Embedded developers possess precise knowledge of their deployment target, including the exact CPU core, available ISA extensions, SRAM allocation, and flash capacity.
ExecuTorch’s ahead-of-time stack is designed to exploit this. ExecuTorch makes target-specific decisions at compile time: graph-level optimizations, memory planning, weight packing, and kernel selection are all target-aware at compile time.
Concretely, for Cortex-M this means:
Graph-level compute elimination. Redundant dtype conversions, quantize/dequantize pairs, and memory format transposes are removed during lowering, so only necessary compute reaches the device.
Quantization parameter folding. Scale and zero-point arithmetic is precomputed into integer multiplier/shift form at export, so quantized kernel inference stays entirely in fixed-point.
AOT weight layout transposition. Convolution weights are transposed from PyTorch’s native layout (OIHW) to CMSIS-NN’s expected format (OHWI) at export time. The permute cost is paid once during compilation and never at inference.
Static memory planning across heterogeneous memories. All tensor and scratch buffers are allocated and laid out ahead of time, with support for spanning multiple memory regions (e.g., TCM and SRAM). Developers can also customize placement to put latency-critical buffers in fast local memory. No heap allocator, no fragmentation, and no runtime memory management required.
Target-specific operator replacement. The CortexMPassManager selects CMSIS-NN kernel variants matched to your core’s ISA tier (Scalar, DSP, or MVE) at compile time, not at runtime.
Developer Workflow
import torch
from torchao.quantization.pt2e.quantize_pt2e import convert_pt2e, prepare_pt2e
from executorch.backends.cortex_m.edge_compile_config import cortex_m_edge_compile_config
from executorch.backends.cortex_m.passes.cortex_m_pass_manager import CortexMPassManager
from executorch.backends.cortex_m.quantizer.quantizer import CortexMQuantizer
from executorch.backends.cortex_m.target_config import CortexM, CortexMTargetConfig
from executorch.exir import to_edge_transform_and_lower
# 1. Export
model = MyModel().eval()
example_inputs = (torch.randn(1, 1, 49, 10),)
exported = torch.export.export(model, example_inputs)
# 2. Quantize and calibrate
quantizer = CortexMQuantizer(use_explicit_layout=True)
prepared = prepare_pt2e(exported.module(), quantizer)
for sample in calibration_data:
prepared(sample)
quantized = convert_pt2e(prepared)
# 3. Re-export the quantized model
quantized_exported = torch.export.export(quantized, example_inputs)
# 4. Lower to Edge and apply the Cortex-M passes
pass_manager = CortexMPassManager(
target_config=CortexMTargetConfig(cpu=CortexM.M55),
use_explicit_layout=True,
)
edge = to_edge_transform_and_lower(
quantized_exported,
compile_config=cortex_m_edge_compile_config(),
transform_passes=pass_manager,
)
# 5. Serialize for integration into firmware
et_program = edge.to_executorch()
with open("model.pte", "wb") as f:
f.write(et_program.buffer)
The resulting .pte binary is linked into firmware alongside the ExecuTorch runtime and CMSIS-NN library, then flashed to the device. At runtime, inference executes the precompiled graph with minimal runtime overhead and no dynamic memory allocation for tensors.
Using the Cortex-M Backend Alongside Ethos-U
Many Cortex-M MCUs pair the CPU with an Arm Ethos-U NPU such as the U55, U65, or U85. ExecuTorch’s EthosUPartitioner delegates supported operations to the NPU via the Vela compiler, and operations left outside the partition run on the Cortex-M CPU within the same graph.
The Cortex-M passes run after Ethos-U partitioning and reuse the quantization parameters already in the graph. This allows a model quantized with EthosUQuantizer to use CMSIS-NN for CPU operations whose quantization, layout and shape constraints meet the Cortex-M backend requirements. Otherwise they fall back to ExecuTorch’s portable kernels, which are functional but not accelerated.
The practical benefit is that NPU operator coverage is not an all-or-nothing gate. A model with a handful of undelegated operations can ship today on mixed CPU/NPU execution, and move more of the graph onto the NPU as coverage grows.
MLPerf Tiny Benchmark Suite
We measured inference latency and memory usage across four of the five MLPerf Tiny Inference benchmark models on the Alif Ensemble E8. These benchmark models represent a set of common deep neural networks representative of TinyML workloads. The Alif E8 integrates multiple Cortex-M55 cores alongside Ethos-U55 and U85 NPUs; we measured on a single M55 high performance core running at 400 MHz, with the Ethos-U NPUs unused. ExecuTorch’s ahead-of-time memory planning means RAM usage is deterministic and bounded, with no fragmentation risk under sustained workloads. ExecuTorch’s operator selective build was used to only include those necessary for inference, creating a minimal flash footprint. All models were INT8 quantized using the CortexMQuantizer and the Alif ML Embedded Evaluation Kit was used as a test harness. These are our own measurements rather than an official MLPerf Tiny submission, so they are not directly comparable to published results on the MLCommons leaderboard.
All four models run in under 90 KiB of RAM, three of them in under 60 KiB, and the anomaly detection autoencoder in 5.2 KiB. Code footprint stays between 15 and 37 KiB because operator selective build links only the operators each model uses.

Demo: Real-time Person Detector
To show what the Cortex-M backend enables in practice, we deployed a µYOLO person detection model on a Renesas EK-RA8D1 board, powered by the Arm Cortex-M85. The deployment fits comfortably within MCU-class memory constraints:
Task: Real-time person detection
Model: µYOLO, pruned depthwise separable CNN backbone with linear predictor head
Model size: 452 KiB (INT8 .pte file)
Total flash: 640 KiB
Peak RAM: 254 KiB
Inference latency: 24 ms per frame inference @ 480 MHz
End-to-end throughput: 12.7 FPS
Input: 128×128 RGB camera frame
This example of resource-constrained, always-on vision on the edge supports applications such as robotics sensing, occupancy monitoring, safety systems, smart cameras, and presence-triggered devices.
Just as importantly, the example demonstrates the development workflow enabled by ExecuTorch. The model definition, training code, export flow, and embedded deployment live within the same PyTorch-based ecosystem. Intermediate representations remain executable, making it possible to compare model outputs throughout export and lowering rather than treating deployment as a black box. The resulting graphs can also be inspected with tools such as Model Explorer, while ETDump exposes per-operator execution costs for profiling on the target. Together, these tools make it possible to iterate on model architecture, accuracy, memory use, and latency while continuously checking that transformations have preserved model behaviour. Instead of exporting a model and only discovering numerical or performance regressions after deployment, developers can inspect and execute intermediate stages of the transformation pipeline.
The model definition, training and export flow are available in the ExecuTorch repository. To facilitate an easy bring-up of the demo without the need for a physical target, the in-tree application is targeted for the Corstone FVP. Board-specific bring-up for the on-device demo was based on code from the ra-fsp-examples repo, configured with the RA Smart Configurator, built using the Arm GNU Toolchain, and flashed using J-Link Flash. For measurements above, the weights of the most expensive operators were placed in DTCM, and the instruction cache was enabled. This resulted in an inference latency reduction from 191 ms to 24 ms, a nearly 8x improvement.

What’s Next
Expanded mixed-precision support. Extending A8W4 and A16W8 mixed-precision support across the full operator set.
Floating-point kernels. CMSIS-NN 8.0.0 introduced fp32 and fp16 MVE kernels. Exposing them via the Cortex-M backend enables non-fully quantized models to use the same lowering path without separate deployment flows.
Broader operator coverage. Adding support for attention operators, layer normalization, and other popular architecture patterns beyond traditional CNNs, along with CMSIS-DSP operators such as FFT so feature extraction can run as part of the graph.
More end-to-end examples. Voice activity detection, gesture recognition, predictive maintenance, and streaming wake word, the fifth MLPerf Tiny benchmark, which needs test infrastructure for multi-frame inference.
Additional hardware validation. Expanding the set of validated platforms and development kits.
We’re excited about what this unlocks for the embedded ML community. If you’re deploying ML at the edge, whether on a $1 sensor node or a Cortex-M55 running voice commands, ExecuTorch now provides a direct path from PyTorch training to on-device inference.

articles.title: Crossing the Gender Binary: Modelling Gendered Reference in Science Fiction and General Fiction
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.19028v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Science fiction is widely credited with unsettling gender. This article asks whether that holds at the linguistic level, in how readily gendered reference gives way to its counterpart, a neutral term, or other social category, and whether it separates the genre from general fiction. It does so by masking man/men, woman/women, and person/people across same-period science fiction and general fiction corpora and classifying RoBERTa's five likeliest substitutes by gender. Retention and displacement are permutation-tested over five resampling rounds, and the underlying sentences are read closely. Both corpora cross the gender binary in both directions, but unequally: where woman is masked, the model predicts a masculine term about twice as often as it predicts a feminine term where man is masked. Each mismatch marks a statistical surprise, a word the corpus did not expect there. Against this shared pattern, science fiction shows greater gender permeability than the general fiction corpus, placing man in feminine contexts more often than general fiction while the reverse rate holds steady. Its degendering tendency is stronger too, drawing both gendered terms toward the neutral. Beyond the binary, a masked woman also draws substitutes naming a social category and no gender far more often than a masked man does. In measuring the gender permeability of man, woman, and person in linguistic distribution and testing whether genre changes it, the study gives science fiction studies linguistic evidence for thematic claims and computational literary studies a pipeline applicable to other category vocabularies, such as race and class.

articles.title: 年轻人开始用AI整顿双11了：算下来能省一大笔钱
articles.text:
快科技10月15日消息，一年一度的“双11”购物节如期而至，各大电商平台的促销广告依旧铺天盖地，直播带货的吆喝声此起彼伏。
今年，你是果断清空购物车，还是佛系旁观？和往年双11买买买不同，今年有的年轻人开始用AI整顿双11了，相关话题引发热议。
一位网友发帖表示，双11那晚脑子一热下了7单，有3样东西到现在都没拆封。后来算了一笔账，这些“伪刚需”花的钱，够买一台不错的平板。今年我换了个打法，开抢前先把购物车扔给AI，让它给我列一份不买清单。
打开购物车，把商品名+价格复制出来，注意别复制收货地址、手机号这些隐私信息，只给商品清单就行，然后一起发给AI助手。
让它按三个维度打分：过去30天用过几次？家里有没有平替？不买会有什么后果？如果AI回答“用不着”，那就直接把商品从清单中移除，过滤掉一些伪刚需，拒绝冲动消费。
利用AI工具来帮助自己找到真实消费需求，勾勒出当下年轻人精打细算的消费新画像。这是消费者认知与市场环境多重因素共同作用的必然结果。
从消费者端看，经过多年的“市场教育”，年轻群体逐渐清醒地认识到“冲动消费”会带来不必要的浪费，年轻人开始回归理性消费。从平台端看，繁琐复杂的满减规则让人望而却步，部分商品“先涨价后降价”的营销套路，也削弱了人们对“双11”的信任感。
如今年轻消费者的理性选择，恰是在提醒各大电商平台：商业的核心竞争力，不是营销噱头，而是透明的价格、优质的服务和可靠的品质。

Existing distributed agent systems typically adopt a disaggregated architecture, deploying different modules on separate devices. While this enables pipeline parallelism, imbalanced module latencies introduce severe pipeline bubbles that limit throughput.
L17: A natural alternative is an aggregated architecture that co-deploys all modules across all devices, eliminating bubbles by keeping every device continuously active. However, this introduces request blocking: short requests are forced to progress in lockstep with longer ones in the same batch, and newly arriving requests must wait until the entire ongoing batch completes the full workflow.

Experiments across four representative agent applications demonstrate that AgentWeave improves throughput by 1.81x, reduces average latency by 2.45x, and reduces P90 latency by 2.04x over state-of-the-art baselines.

articles.title: Retrieve What Helps, Only When It Helps: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Machine Translation
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.19528v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Retrieving external knowledge can improve large language model (LLM) translation by providing supplementary information such as idiom interpretations and terminology. However, existing retrieval-augmented machine translation systems typically apply predefined retrieval strategies uniformly across all inputs. We argue that translation operates in a partial-evidence regime: LLM's parametric knowledge suffices for many inputs, while external evidence benefits a subset and usually supports rather than directly provides the desired translation. This creates two challenges: deciding when to retrieve and what evidence to acquire. We introduce Selective Retrieval-Augmented Translation (SRAT), an agentic reinforcement learning framework that learns when to translate directly or retrieve, what to retrieve, and how to integrate these decisions by optimizing final translation quality. To align evidence retrieval with downstream translation quality rather than simple semantic similarity, we further develop joint Plackett--Luce optimization and translation-quality contrastive training for retriever-training. Experiments on idiom, knowledge-intensive, and document-level translation with offline or online retrieval show that SRAT consistently outperforms never- and always-retrieve baselines, and quality-aligned retriever training provides further gains when similarity-based retrieval is insufficient. The results demonstrate the benefit of treating retrieval as a learnable translation action rather than fixed preprocessing.

articles.title: Anthropic 抛弃 Git，选择自研版本控制系统 Scion
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，美国人工智能公司 Anthropic 近日宣布弃用 Git，转为采用自研的版本控制系统 Scion，将大部分源代码管理操作转移至服务器，减少智能体和自动化任务需要下载的数据。
Anthropic 表示，公司 5 月平均每天合并 2500 次代码变更；到了 9 月，这一数字已经超过 3 万次，Git 已经无法满足需求，为此公司选择自研 Scion 系统。
Anthropic 宣称，Scion 的 CPU 和内存消耗仅为 Git 的两百分之一。切换系统后，CI 和研究任务代码检出操作仅需几秒钟，不再是之前的几分钟。
IT之家了解到，Scion 将提交、合并、变基和文件历史查询等操作放在服务器端执行，客户端负责跟踪本地修改、管理文件，并维护有限的缓存，无需保存足够多的仓库数据就能独立完成上述操作。
Anthropic 表示，他们的大部分客户端都是始终保持在线的智能体，因此 Git 离线支持并没有什么优势。将操作集中到服务器端，可以减少本地存储需求和同步开销。当然其他公司也很难采用这种操作，因为它需要配套的定制代码审查、搜索和 CI 工具。

articles.title: GPT-6-Astra solves 49 of 50 physics research problems at $2.40 apiece
articles.text:
On the TheoPhysEval benchmark, GPT-6-Astra solves 49 of 50 unpublished theoretical physics calculations as accurately as leading specialists. In some cases where the agent seemed to fail, the experts' own reference solutions turned out to contain errors. But the researchers say physics hasn't had a breakthrough like the ones in mathematics, because the agents lack "taste." They still think autonomous, top-level AI research could arrive soon. They already see consequences for how young physicists are trained and for equal opportunity in the field.
The article GPT-6-Astra solves 49 of 50 physics research problems at $2.40 apiece appeared first on The Decoder.

articles.title: The Sum of All Summaries: PROPALIGN for Graded Proposition Salience Evaluation
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.19387v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Identification and ranking of salient propositions in documents is indirectly involved in many AI tasks, but few papers define proposition salience scores clearly, make diverse data available, or evaluate models directly on the task. This paper proposes PROPALIGN, a multiple-summary-based approach for propositional salience score estimation, and releases PROPALIGNBANK, an accompanying dataset for the method with 138K alignments of over 35K propositions. We compare several approaches to salient proposition extraction in English across a broad range of spoken and written genres, and demonstrate that naively asking models for judgments leads to inconsistencies. By contrast, graded, summary-based metrics are more stable. We further observe that while single models perform worse than humans, an ensemble of models incorporating linguistic features approaches manual annotation quality ceilings. In addition, analyses of the model outputs suggest insights into how models can extract salient information with and without the use of summaries.

articles.title: NEPSEE: A Double-Annotated Benchmark for Nepali Sentiment Analysis
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.19190v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Many sentiment datasets use one annotator for each item, so the test labels show the conventions of that person. We build a Nepali benchmark from two annotators who labelled the same sentences blind. They labelled 5,614 sentences from tweets of Nepali public figures on a five-point scale. We keep only the 3,189 sentences where both give the same polarity. On the three-class benchmark, NepBERTa with a fixed tokenizer gets a macro-F1 of 0.877 and IndicBERTv2 0.867. Three commercial large language models (LLMs) get 0.882 to 0.896 zero-shot, and these differences are not significant. On the five-point scale, 766 sentences have two adjacent labels, for example Pos and SPos. We accept both labels and train on both. On this task, Claude Opus 5.5 beats the best encoders by 0.10 to 0.12 macro-F1. A tokenizer audit adds a second result. The default tokenizers of three Nepali BERT models delete the non-spacing Devanagari vowel signs and the virama. When we restore the marks, macro-F1 increases by 0.084 for NepBERTa but decreases by 0.095 for a model pretrained on stripped text.

articles.title: Intel 18A工艺就用了 台积电回应High NA EUV光刻机落后
articles.text:
快科技10月15日消息，ASML的EUV光刻机正在从当前的Low NA EUV转向High NA EUV，单台价格也会从2亿美元提升到4亿美元左右，但这次首发的不再是台积电。
在High NA EUV光刻机上，Intel公司后来居上，之前计划是14A工艺上采用，现在已经在去年底量产的18A工艺上使用了，这个进度比其他厂商领先4-5年以上。
台积电这次对High NA EUV光刻机的态度很保守，要知道他们是全球第一个量产EUV工艺的，早在2018年的7nm工艺上就率先导入EUV光刻了——当年三星比台积电官宣量产EUV的时间早，但三星的没啥产出，市场还是公认台积电最早量产EUV。
正因为此，台积电对High NA EUV的保守态度也引发了关注，他们公布的计划是2030年才开始导入这种工艺。
在日前的财报会议上台积电再次回应了他们为何不率先采购High NA EUV光刻机的原因，表示台积电选择在2030年开始采用，是因为公司认为届时High NA技术将足够成熟。
台积电声称，目前正与ASML紧密合作，计划在2031年前确立12英寸光罩标准，届时台积电认为High NA的成本将达到适合台积电投入量产的合理水平，这是一项非常出色的工具，在更小的几何尺寸上无疑能带来优势。
至于台积电比竞争对手更晚采用是否会对台积电构成劣势，台积电表示他们坚信自己依然是为客户提供最先进技术的领先企业。
从台积电的回应来看，不率先采用High NA EUV的原因其实就是2个，一个是贵，High NA EUV光刻机自身贵，工艺成本也贵。
第二个原因跟High NA EUV的缺陷有关，我们之前提到过这一点，当前的Low NA EUV光刻机能生产大约800mm2的大芯片，而High NA EUV因为视场的原因，生产的芯片面积减半到400mm2左右，做不了大型AI芯片。
这需要更先进的光罩技术，这就是台积电上面说的跟ASML公司合作研发12英寸光罩标准的事，这个问题解决了才能生产大型AI芯片，High NA EUV才有量产的意义。

articles.title: 《猎天使魔女》DLSS 5贝姐变熟女 面部大变样！
articles.text:
近日，一名玩家尝试将英伟达DLSS 5神经网络渲染技术应用于2009年发售的《猎天使魔女》，并通过一系列工具将其整合进这款经典游戏中。
作者表示，在特定画质设置下，帧率最高可提升至原来的两倍，让RTX 5060级别的显卡能够以2K分辨率稳定运行在60帧。为了适配这项技术，作者还借助ReShade的Shader Toggler插件调整了游戏的后期处理效果，关闭原版的阶梯状雾效滤镜和画面去饱和处理，并通过自定义LUT校正曝光与色彩。
开启神经网络渲染后，游戏中的环境和角色服装呈现出更明显的纹理细节，包括布料、皮革以及哥特式建筑的石材质感。不过，主角贝优妮塔的面部也被AI重新处理，颧骨、下颌线和法令纹等细节均发生变化。
相关演示公开后，引发玩家对画面风格变化和AI生成瑕疵的讨论。部分网友认为改进过的面部特征也带来了明显的“恐怖谷”观感。
此次演示使用的DLSS 5并非NVIDIA正式发布的版本，非官方修改也可能存在兼容性等问题。
因此，目前网络上展示的画质和性能表现，并不能代表DLSS 5正式版本的最终效果。

articles.title: Nvidia RTX 5090 disappears from Micro Center amid rumors of a production halt
articles.text:
Buying a GeForce RTX 5090, widely regarded as one of the best graphics cards on the market, was already extremely difficult because of price hikes and near-zero availability. Now, it will be impossible to get one. Amid recent rumors that Nvidia is halting production of the GeForce RTX 5090, another sign of the card's disappearance from the U.S. market are emerging. Micro Center has reclassified the Blackwell flagship as "Not Carried," and many of its stores have sold out. Tom's Hardware has reached out to Micro Center for comment.
Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs
(Image credit: Noctua)
Desktop GPU Roadmap
Nvidia's Enterprise GPU Roadmap
Testing DirectStorage with GPU decompression
The GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?
Rubin in-depth

The “not carried” status on a product is different from simply being out of stock. When an item is out of stock, it just means the product is temporarily unavailable, but the retailer plans to restock once new inventory arrives from the manufacturer. In contrast, a "not carried" label implies the product is no longer part of the retailer's active catalog. Therefore, the retailer does not expect to restock the item.
Custom GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards from Nvidia partners such as Asus, MSI, and Gigabyte are still listed on Micro Center’s website for now. However, a closer look shows these models are out of stock at all of the retailer’s physical locations. This widespread unavailability lends credence to the rumors that Nvidia has reportedly stopped producing the GeForce RTX 5090.
The Asus GeForce RTX 5090 ROG Astral Edition 20 is the only GeForce RTX 5090 graphics card that remains in stock at most Micro Center stores nationwide. However, there is a catch. This particular model is only available as part of the exclusive Asus ROG 20th Anniversary Bundle priced at almost $11,000.
(Image credit: Micro Center)
Adding another twist to the unfolding story, one Redditor claimed to have seen Micro Center employees remove all GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards from the shelves on October 9, just a day before rumors of a production halt began circulating online. According to the account, when the Redditor asked the store manager why, the manager refused to explain.
The Redditor wanted to buy the Asus ProArt GeForce RTX 5090; however, a Micro Center employee reportedly said the graphics card "was pulled and being sent somewhere else," offering no further explanation. Nonetheless, the Redditor noticed two GeForce RTX 5090 cards still on the shelf and allegedly begged staff to let them buy one. The Asus GeForce RTX 5090 ROG Astral Edition 20 would require selling a kidney, and no doctor or surgical equipment was nearby. Therefore, the Redditor bought the Gigabyte GeForce RTX 5090 Aorus Stealth Ice, which Micro Center generously price-matched to the cheaper Asus ProArt GeForce RTX 5090.
The fairytale ending wrapped up with the Micro Center employee reportedly telling the customer, "congrats on getting the last 5090 we will probably sell..."Bought the last 5090 at my Microcenter from r/Microcenter
Nvidia has not officially commented on the GeForce RTX 5090's situation. Despite ongoing speculation, the chipmaker still lists the GeForce RTX 5090 on its website with a “starting at $1,999” price, an MSRP we have not seen in ages. The original rumor suggested that Nvidia had stopped producing the GeForce RTX 5090, but it has not been formally confirmed as a discontinuation.
It makes sense for Nvidia to reallocate the GB202 silicon that powers the GeForce RTX 5090 into its Pro lineup, where profit margins are considerably higher. Instead of focusing on the GeForce RTX 5090 for gaming, Nvidia can channel the GB202 into products like the RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell, RTX Pro 5500, and RTX Pro 5000, where the market will pay a steep premium for the same silicon.
Sadly, times are changing, and the GeForce RTX 5090 has shifted from flagship to a soon-unattainable halo product.

articles.title: From Qualitative Text to Integrated Evidence: The Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI) Procedure
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.19164v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Mixed methods research offers established strategies for integrating qualitative and quantitative evidence, but less guidance for integrating two computational representations of the same qualitative corpus. This methodological study introduces Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI), a four-step procedure for explicit and traceable integration. We present PTI using 1,203 interview paragraphs from 29 mothers in Nepal. The two representations were ontology-guided Patient Voice (PV) coding with PVminer and data-driven themes generated through non-negative matrix factorization (NMF). A theme-complete crosswalk documented convergence, divergence, and preprocessing-sensitive differences. Depression status, based on Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores, served as a secondary external anchor for exploratory association checks. PTI provides a structured approach for integrating computational representations of qualitative text within mixed methods research.

articles.title: Cursor Staff Investigated Whether Confidential Data Reached SpaceX for AI Training
articles.text:
In the weeks before SpaceX’s AI unit in August introduced Grok Bot, its version of a personal AI agent, engineers at Cursor discovered a potential problem.
Cursor, the AI coding startup SpaceX was then in the process of acquiring, was developing Grok Bot, and as part of that process, employees across Cursor were using the tool extensively for testing and as a part of their everyday work. In late July, engineers raised concerns that Cursor might have sent data from that internal testing—potentially including confidential information about its customers, suppliers and business partners—to SpaceX’s AI unit. One of Cursor’s lawyers warned that if word got out that the company was using the data for training, that could cause a “huge trust problem,” according to internal communications viewed by The Information.

articles.title: What’s new with Google Data Cloud
articles.text:
October 12 - October 16
Looker Data Apps are now in Preview to build and host interactive, agent-generated applications natively inside Looker
Generated using natural language prompts, the Antigravity CLI, or Claude Code, these interactive web applications, natively hosted inside Looker, transform business reporting into operational systems of action. Users can test scenarios, adjust parameters, and trigger workflows in downstream platforms while inheriting LookML semantic modeling, row-level security, and access controls with no runtime LLM token costs. Read the announcement blog.
Build end-to-end data science pipelines with the Data Agent Kit
Following the general availability of the Data Agent Kit, a new end-to-end walkthrough demonstrates how data teams can build, test, and schedule machine learning pipelines directly from their preferred code editors. Explore the walkthrough and codelab.
Manage dashboard agents as code to bring CI/CD and version control to LookML dashboards
Data teams can now declare agent parameters, configurations, and prompt instructions alongside dashboard files in code. This integration enables standard developer workflows for conversational BI, including Git version control, peer review, branching, and automated CI/CD validation before agent modifications reach production end users. Read the technical guide on the Google Developer Community.
Simplify AI search with native AlloyDB hybrid search and Reciprocal Rank Fusion
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL simplifies hybrid search architectures by combining vector similarity search and keyword BM25 retrieval within a unified database engine. Using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), developers can merge lexical scoring and semantic embeddings into a single ranked result without writing a complex SQL query. This unified approach removes the operational overhead of running and synchronizing external search engines alongside operational databases for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and search applications. Explore hybrid search in AlloyDB.
October 5 - October 9
Data Agent Kit is now generally available to bring Google Data Cloud to any coding agent
Data Agent Kit provides a free collection of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools and Google-authored agent skills that connect more than 15 Google Data Cloud services directly to coding agents across VS Code, Antigravity, Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex. This release expands support for developers and data practitioners to inspect schemas, author queries, and build end-to-end data pipelines in natural language directly from their IDE or CLI. Read the announcement blog.
Spanner Omni is now generally available for deploy-anywhere, multi-model workloads
Spanner Omni brings Spanner's distributed SQL, graph, vector, and key-value capabilities to any environment, including on-premises data centers, other public clouds via Kubernetes or VMs, and local developer laptops. Organizations can build and run multi-model applications with consistent APIs and query engines across hybrid and multi-cloud footprints while seamlessly scaling to managed Spanner on Google Cloud. Read the launch blog and explore how Spanner also removed cumulative mutation limits for DML transactions.
AlloyDB delivers PostgreSQL for agents and native BM25 hybrid search
We announced PostgreSQL for agents in AlloyDB, introducing an agentic database architecture engineered for real-time data access at agent scale with workload isolation. In addition, native BM25 ranking is now in Preview for AlloyDB and Cloud SQL, allowing developers to combine keyword search and vector embeddings directly in PostgreSQL without maintaining an external search engine. For hybrid deployments, the AlloyDB Omni RPM Orchestrator is now generally available, and you can dive deeper in our new Build AI apps and agents with AlloyDB eBook.
Lakehouse runtime catalog adds regional endpoints across 22 regions and GA support for flexible column names
Lakehouse runtime catalog regional endpoints are now live across 22 Google Cloud regions across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Middle East, supporting both the Apache Iceberg REST catalog endpoint and the Apache Hive catalog endpoint to help customers meet strict data residency and sovereignty requirements. In addition, flexible column names for Apache Iceberg tables are now generally available by default across Iceberg external tables and managed tables, enabling seamless querying of columns containing spaces, hyphens, and Unicode characters. We also announced the Preview of cross-cloud caching and connections for the borderless Lakehouse.
Unlock predictive and agent-ready insights with BigQuery augmented analytics TVFs, TabFM, and identity columns
BigQuery introduced augmented analytics table-valued functions (TVFs): six built-in functions that automate metric diagnostics, trend analysis, and pattern discovery directly where your data lives and integrate as skills for AI agents. We also introduced TabFM in BigQuery to bring tabular foundation model capabilities to predictive analytics, alongside BigQuery identity columns to automatically generate sequential surrogate keys and simplify data warehouse pipelines.
Dataflow adds Pause/Resume and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU support for large-scale AI workloads
New Dataflow capabilities make it easier to run high-throughput streaming and batch AI pipelines at scale, including Pause/Resume job controls and support for NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. Customer momentum across Google Data Cloud — Yahoo, PayPal, Surescripts, Airwallex, and Lucius AI
Organizations across industries are scaling their data and AI foundations on Google Data Cloud. Yahoo uses flexible VMs in Managed Service for Apache Spark to reduce provisioning failures by 85%, while PayPal migrated mission-critical analytics workloads to Managed Service for Apache Spark to scale and reduce operational overhead. On the database front, Surescripts migrated 30.5 billion annual healthcare transactions to AlloyDB with 99.998% uptime, Airwallex manages more than 5,000 databases with 99.99% availability on Cloud SQL with a team of four DBAs, and Lucius AI runs a 210,000-tender global platform on AlloyDB and MCP with 47x faster ScaNN vector search.
September 7 - September 10
Pub/Sub SMTs can now AI Inference your Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform models!
Pub/Sub AI Inference SMTs allow you to apply inference on an incoming stream of events using models hosted in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. The model’s prediction is appended to your event, making it available for downstream processing in your data warehouse (like BigQuery) or operational database (like BigTable). This feature, now generally available, can dramatically simplify or enhance anomaly detection systems you are operating.
PostgreSQL Source Connector is now generally available in Managed Service for Apache Kafka!
Managed Service for Apache Kafka’s PostgreSQL connector allows customers to capture changes from their PostgreSQL database and ingest them into their Kafka infrastructure with low latency. This source connector is compatible with Cloud SQL for Postgres, AlloyDB, and self-managed PostgreSQL databases. Try this along with our entire portfolio of managed connectors, including MirrorMaker 2.0, BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and Pub/Sub! E-mail kafka-hotline@google.com if you have questions or feedback!
Pause-on-failure for Dataflow batch jobs is GA
Dataflow pause-on-failure enables you to preserve the state of a batch Dataflow job before it fails. By pausing your Dataflow job, you can address issues that are external to the pipeline and resume processing without losing completed work. This helps you better manage resource costs and improve job reliability when you face temporary outages or capacity constraints.
The insertAll API is now the BigQuery Storage Write API (REST)
The legacy insertAll streaming API is now rebranded as the BigQuery Storage Write API (REST). By dropping the "legacy" label, developers can confidently build long-term HTTP-based streaming workflows. This stateless JSON-over-HTTPS endpoint offers a lightweight alternative to heavy gRPC libraries—ideal for serverless web apps, IoT telemetry, and AI logging. The transition is seamless for existing users, requiring zero code changes and offering 100% backward compatibility. However, the Storage Write API (gRPC) version remains the recommended standard for high-throughput, continuous pipelines.
August 31 - September 4
Stateful processing is available in BigQuery continuous queries in Preview
Stateful operations significantly expand what’s possible with BigQuery continuous queries. This feature allows users to leverage functions like JOINs, aggregations, and windowing functions directly in their streaming queries. Now you can calculate metrics over time (for example, a 30-minute average) to power your downstream applications and AI agents with much richer, real-time signals.
Try out our feature here and share your feedback with bq-continuous-queries-feedback@google.com!
Synthetic data generator tool is available for Managed Service for Kafka
You’ve launched your first Kafka cluster. Now what? The next thing to do is to produce some data to the cluster, but that involves modifying a client application somewhere or spinning up a virtual machine. The synthetic data generator tool, now generally available, can start sending mock data to your cluster in 3 clicks, and will get data streaming into your cluster in less than two minutes. The perfect utility for those moments you just want to test your cluster and new features. Try our quickstart today!
Dataflow pipeline updates are faster & more flexible
Dataflow pipeline updates can now stop-and-replace pipelines, a major addition to the existing in-place-update feature. The new parallel pipeline option accelerates the migration between the old & new pipeline, resulting in reduced disruption to your business. You can also set a timeout on drains that prevents runaway costs for your pipeliness in the event of stuck processing. This feature is generally available. Try it here!
July 6 - July 10
New Lakehouse managed tables now in preview
Lakehouse tables for Apache Iceberg are now in preview and available in the console. By using Google-managed Apache Iceberg tables in Lakehouse, you can eliminate the overhead of maintaining duplicate data pipelines and complex synchronization logic between BigQuery and open-source engines. This unified table format delivers native, multi-engine read and write interoperability, allowing you to run concurrent DML/DDL operations across diverse analytics tools on a single, shared storage layer.  Built-in automated table management handles painful background optimization tasks like compaction and partition tuning, freeing up your team to focus on building rather than managing storage maintenance.

articles.title: Why AI-Written Software Needs a Flight Simulator
articles.text:
As companies create more applications using AI, corporate officers say demand is rising for a new type of software that stress-tests those apps, simulating how they handle network problems and other disasters that humans may not think to test for—including cyberattacks by rogue AIs.
Luis Chávez, CTO of coding assistant provider Replit, says his company uses an AI-assisted software known as a deterministic simulator, a kind of flight simulator for software. The deterministic part refers to how the simulator lets companies run the same disaster test again and again so they can try out different fixes for bugs that crop up during network failures or hacking attempts.
Traditional stress-testing methods rely on developers guessing every potential problem that may arise. Merely using today’s AI models to evaluate code often produces false alarms or fake warnings, corporate executives say.

articles.title: 苹果营销主管谈 OpenAI 硬件：我们没感到有威胁，相比追逐 AGI 更重视用户隐私与日常使用体验
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，除了苹果 CEO 约翰・特努斯（John Ternus）之外，《时代》今日还采访到了苹果全球营销高级副总裁格雷格・乔斯维亚克（Greg Joswiak）。
当谈及 OpenAI 的硬件计划时，他表示，苹果并不担心 OpenAI 进军硬件领域带来的竞争。“我们并未感受到威胁。我们能够实现这样的软硬件整合，这意味着我们可以创造比其他任何人都更好的体验。”
乔斯维亚克还谈到了苹果对人工智能产品的定位。他表示，苹果并不是专门为那些执着于追求超级智能的 AI 爱好者开发产品。“我们欢迎他们使用我们的产品，但他们不是我们的目标用户。我们的目标是让普通人的日常生活变得更好。”
《时代》指出，苹果虽然正在训练自有 AI 模型，但在前沿 AI 技术方面仍与行业领先者存在差距。苹果高管并未将重点放在追逐 AGI 上，而是强调打造个性化、注重隐私且能够帮助普通用户的 AI 体验。
乔斯维亚克将部分狂热 AI 追随者称为“lunatic fringe”（IT之家注：常用来指代少数极端分子、狂热派或少数顽固派），并以此与苹果面向日常用户的产品定位作对比。
苹果长期强调硬件、软件和服务之间的整合能力。乔斯维亚克表示，公司认为，通过整合设备、操作系统和服务，可以提供具有差异化的用户体验。
与此同时，OpenAI 正在探索硬件产品，但其具体产品形态及市场表现仍有待观察。
